methodology: Use only the minimum dataset features: mu, sigma, liquidity, and cost.
Normalize those features and construct a transparent decision score.
Infer weight bands and compare them with the final optimized decision variables x.
Classify assets as accepted or rejected based on the final feasible solution.
decision_analysis.summary: The model first normalizes expected return, volatility, liquidity, and cost onto a common [0, 1] scale. It then computes a transparent score that rewards higher return and liquidity, rewards lower volatility, and penalizes higher cost. The top assets by that score are Asset 3, Asset 7, Asset 4. Those assets receive wider allocation bands, while lower-ranked assets are assigned tighter satellite bands or near-zero weight bands.

explanation.objective_function: Minimize x^T Sigma_hat x - 1.000 mu^T x + 0.150 C(x) - 0.350 L(x) + 0.450 CVaR_0.950(x) + 0.300 D_gap(x) + 0.180 HHI(x) + 0.280 Omega_regime(x) + 0.120 T(x), with Sigma_hat using shrinkage phi=0.000. HYBRID behaves as progressive and balanced search.
solver_steps: Solve a QP baseline, refine with PSO, mutate with GA, then form an adaptive hybrid consensus solution.
Form the return vector mu, covariance matrix Sigma, and shrinkage-adjusted covariance Sigma_hat.
Assemble liquidity, transaction-cost, CVaR-scenario, and regime-conditioned tensors.
Set the objective and enforce nonnegative weights that sum to 1.
Solve the model-specific optimization problem.
Project the solution back to the feasible simplex if needed.
Validate the allocation and compute summary metrics.

mathematical_model.normalization_equation: f_tilde_i(x) = ( f_i(x) - min f_i ) / ( max f_i - min f_i )
mathematical_model.objective_equation: J(x)=x^T Sigma_hat x-lambda mu^T x+gamma c^T x-delta l^T x+theta CVaR_alpha(x)+kappa( sum x_i^2-1/K )^2+psi sum x_i^2+rho Omega_regime(x)+omega||x-x_ref||_2^2
mathematical_model.return_engine_equation: mu_BL=[(tau Sigma)^-1+P^T Omega^-1 P]^-1[(tau Sigma)^-1 pi+P^T Omega^-1 q], with Bayesian shrinkage used to form the view vector q
mathematical_model.exact_cvar_seed_equation: min_{x,eta,u} x^T Sigma_hat x-lambda mu^T x+theta[eta+(1/(1-alpha)N)sum u_t]+... s.t. u_t>=-r_t^T x-eta, u_t>=0, c^T x<=B, 0<=x_i<=alpha_bar, sum x_i=1
mathematical_model.regime_equation: Omega_regime(x)=0.65 Var_p(mu_s^T x)+0.35 E_p[x^T Sigma_s x]
mathematical_model.dynamic_policy_equation: x_t*=arg min_x J_t(x) over a rolling lookback window with receding-horizon re-optimization
mathematical_model.scalarization_note: Scalarization converts the multi-objective portfolio problem into a single-objective optimization problem.
mathematical_model.relaxed_real_estate_model: x_i in [0,1]  (continuous relaxation used for tractable optimization)
constraints: active asset count approx equals K through projection

theoretical_properties.title: Proposition 1 (Stability)
theoretical_properties.statement: Shrinkage covariance with diagonal regularization makes Sigma_hat positive definite in the implemented model, so the quadratic risk block is strictly convex.
theoretical_properties.interpretation: This improves numerical stability, keeps the Hessian well-conditioned, and supports reliable local optimization.

theoretical_properties.title: Proposition 2 (Hybrid Convergence)
theoretical_properties.statement: Under bounded objective values, finite projected search space, and best-so-far retention in the hybrid pipeline, the QP-PSO-GA stack admits convergence to a stationary candidate point.
theoretical_properties.interpretation: This is a heuristic stationary-point claim for the hybrid search, not a guarantee of global optimality.

theoretical_properties.title: Proposition 3 (Return Stabilization)
theoretical_properties.statement: Bayesian/Black-Litterman return estimation shrinks noisy asset-level return views toward a market-implied prior, reducing estimation error sensitivity in mu.
theoretical_properties.interpretation: This does not guarantee higher realized return, but it typically improves robustness of the optimizer by preventing unstable weights driven by noisy point estimates.

coherent_risk_theory.headline: CVaR is treated as a coherent risk measure.
coherent_risk_theory.research_note: Using CVaR instead of variance alone strengthens theoretical credibility in downside-risk modeling.

decision_variables.meaning: VaR/CVaR threshold variable used in the tail-risk interpretation
